Marine animals of Galiano Island (1893–2021) A catalogue of the marine animals reported from the waters around Galiano Island, from sponges and worms to fishes and marine mammals, bringing together historical collections and published reports with the community science observations gathered by the Biodiversity Galiano project since 2016. Records distinguish historical reports that have since been confirmed, those that remain unconfirmed, and species newly reported for the island.
Data paper: Simon et al. (2022), Biodiversity Data Journal 10: e76050
View dataset →
Diatoms of the Salish Sea (1866–2026) A catalogue of marine diatom occurrences across the Salish Sea, consolidating records from the published literature, morphological study of samples and molecular (DNA metabarcoding) surveys. Together, these records document the region’s diatom flora and how knowledge of it has accumulated since the first reports in 1866.
Data paper: Webber et al. (2026), Biodiversity Data Journal 14: e189060
View dataset →

Our approach to detecting biodiversity change is documented in the Protocol for the Detection of Extirpation, which walks through our framework for inferring local extinction using a tutorial dataset from Galiano Island. The protocol is described in full in our article in Plants, People, Planet. Aspects of this protocol have been adapted in the bioReportR framework, with examples presented here for the Átl’ḵa7tsem/Howe Sound Biosphere and Saanich Peninsula.

Flora of the Saanich Peninsula An analysis of the vascular plant flora of the Saanich Peninsula, drawing on historical collections and community science observations to map the status of the region’s plants, track species that have not been reported in recent decades, and recognise the contributors whose records make this work possible. We are grateful for funding provided by the Sitka Foundation, the Canadian Institute of Ecology and Evolution, the Capital Regional District, Nature Victoria, and Keefer Ecological Services Ltd. in support of this project.
Visit project site →
Átl’ḵa7tsem/Howe Sound Biosphere Vegetation Report A map-based report on the vascular plant diversity of the Átl’ḵa7tsem/Howe Sound Biosphere Region, relating historical and community science records to biogeoclimatic zones and protected areas across the biosphere. Visit project site →
Protocol for the Detection of Extirpation Developed on Galiano Island, this protocol for detecting local extinction, or extirpation, combines historical specimens, community science observations and targeted searches. Weighing the search effort spent in each species' historical and potential habitat, the protocol tests the hypothesis that a population has been lost, in line with IUCN extinction criteria. Published in Plants, People, Planet. Visit project site →
